chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How did the waiting period of the divorced woman become three menstruations, or three months, and the waiting period of the woman whose husband died become four months and ten days?'
So he said: 'As for the waiting period of the divorced woman being three pure periods (Quroo'), it is for the clearing of the womb from the child.'

And as for the waiting period of the woman whose husband died, indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stipulated a condition for the women and stipulated a condition against them. So He did not seize them with what He stipulated for them, nor was He unjust with what He stipulated against them.

He stipulated for them regarding the oath (of abstention from intercourse) four months, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'For those who swear to abstain from their wives, [let them have] a waiting period of four months.'
So He did not allow anyone more than four months regarding the oath, for His knowledge, Blessed and High, knows that it is the limit of the woman's patience from the man.
And as for what He stipulated against them, then He commanded her that she should observe a waiting period when her husband dies from her, for four months and ten days.
Thus, He took from her for him at his death what He took for her from him during his life at the time of his oath.
Allah, Blessed and High, says: 'They should keep themselves in waiting for four months and ten.'
And He did not mention the ten days in the waiting period except with the four months.
And He knew that the limit of the woman's patience is the four months regarding the abstention from intercourse.
So from that, He obligated it against her and for her.

key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: Waiting period of the divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind the difference between the waiting period of a divorced woman and a widowed woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the three-month 'Iddah for divorce serves primarily for 'Istibra' (clearing the womb), whereas the extended four-month-and-ten-day period for widowhood reflects a divine balance of reciprocity. This duration is rooted in the principle that Allah limited the maximum period of an oath of abstention (Ila') to four months, thereby establishing the upper limit of a woman's patience for sexual abstinence, which He then extended by ten days for the widow's mourning period.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Husayn Bin Sayf, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2nd, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How come the waiting period of the divorced woman is three menstruations, or three months, and the waiting period of the woman widowed from her husband came to be four months and ten (days)?’
So heasws said: ‘As for the waiting period of the divorced woman being three Quroos (pure periods), so it is for the freeing of the womb from the child,

and as for the waiting period of the woman widowed from her husband, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Stipulated a condition for the women, and Stipulated a condition against them. So He<sup>azwj</sup> did not Seize them with regards to what He<sup>azwj</sup> stipulated for the, and was not Unjust with regards to what He<sup>azwj</sup> Stipulated against them.

A condition for them regarding the oath (by the husband not to copulate) is four months as Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [2:226] Those who swear that they will not go in to their wives should wait four months.
Thus, it is not allowed for anyone, more than four months regarding the oath, for the Blessed and High Knows that it is the limit of the patient of the woman from the man.
And as for what He<sup>azwj</sup> Stipulated against them, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Commanded her that she should wait, when her husband dies from her, for four months and ten (days).
Thus, He<sup>azwj</sup> Took from her for him during his death, what he Took for her from him during his lifetime with the oathing.
Allahazwj Says [2:234] they should keep themselves in waiting for four months and ten,
and did not Mention the ‘ten days’ in the waiting period except with the four months,
and Knows that the limit of the patience of the woman is four months regarding the neglect of the copulation,
So from then it Obligates against her and for her’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Muhammad ibn Sulayman who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, al-Thaniy, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, why is it that waiting period for a woman divorced three times, is three cycles of Hayd (menses) or three months, and the waiting period of a widow is four months and ten days?
He (the Imam) said, ‘Waiting period for a woman divorced three times is passing of three Hayd (menses)- free periods. It is to ascertain a womb is free of child and pregnancy.

About the waiting period of a widow Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has set a condition for and a condition against women. In the condition for them He does not hold them accountable and in the condition against them He has not done injustice to them.

In the case of ’Ila’ (swearing not to go to bed with one’s wife) it is four months as Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, ‘. . . for those who swear there is a four month waiting period.’ [2:226]
He has not made it permissible for anyone in the case of ‘Ila’ to wait more than four months because He, most Blessed, most High, knows how long women can wait without going to bed and without men.
The condition against women is in the case of the death of their husband in which case they must wait for four months and ten days.
Thus He has taken from her when he dies as much as He has takes for her from him during his life time in the case of ‘Ila’
as Allah, most Blessed, most High, says, ‘. . . they must wait for four months and ten days.’
He has not mentioned the ten days in waiting period except with four months.
He knows that women can wait without men only for four months and without going to bed.
For this reason He has set conditions for and against them.’”
